schema.title: Identity
schema.description: North-star professional identity and durable positioning knowledge.

identity.headline: Technical Content Strategist, Journalist, SEO Specialist, AI Workflow Builder
identity.professionalMission: Help people understand complex ideas through thoughtful communication, practical systems, and emerging technology.
identity.northStar: Become the person who understands meaningful technological change before most people and translates it into practical value for businesses, creators, and readers.
identity.identityStatement: Riley Wallace is not defined by a single profession. Journalism, marketing, technical writing, SEO, automation, AI, strategy, and design are all expressions of the same underlying skill: solving communication problems. His work consistently revolves around making complicated ideas understandable, useful, and interesting.

careerNarrative.summary: Throughout his career Riley has repeatedly moved into emerging fields before they became mainstream. Rather than specializing in one job title, he specializes in learning quickly, connecting ideas across disciplines, and creating systems that help other people understand complexity.

careerEvolution.purpose: Learn research, interviewing, storytelling and editorial thinking.
Understand business strategy, audience behaviour and measurable outcomes.
Translate highly technical subjects into content that people can actually understand.
Move beyond producing content into building systems that create, organize and improve knowledge.

careerNarrative.commonTheme: Every career transition has been motivated by curiosity rather than titles. New technology represents an opportunity to learn and create rather than something to fear.

secondary: Document knowledge instead of repeatedly recreating it.

professionalIdentityTraits.description: Naturally investigates subjects in depth and enjoys understanding how things work.
Looks for repeatable frameworks instead of one-off solutions.
Looks for the interesting human story hidden inside technical and business topics.
Prefers creating tools and systems over repeatedly performing manual work.
Enjoys helping people understand concepts they previously found intimidating.

coreValues.name: Curiosity
coreValues.statement: Learning compounds over time. Curiosity is Riley's greatest long-term competitive advantage.
evidence: Career transitions consistently follow emerging technology.
Actively explores new tools before they become mainstream.
Enjoys documentaries, mysteries, obscure music and deep technical subjects.

coreValues.name: Clarity
coreValues.statement: If something cannot be explained clearly, it probably is not fully understood.

coreValues.name: Integrity
coreValues.statement: Evidence matters more than hype. Never exaggerate accomplishments or misrepresent expertise.

coreValues.name: Adaptability
coreValues.statement: The future belongs to people who adapt quickly rather than defend old ways of working.

coreValues.name: Generosity
coreValues.statement: Knowledge becomes more valuable when shared.

operatingPrinciples.title: Build systems instead of repeating work.
operatingPrinciples.description: Whenever possible, replace repetitive manual effort with a reusable process.

operatingPrinciples.title: Document everything worth remembering.
operatingPrinciples.description: Knowledge should become permanent assets rather than disappear after a project.

operatingPrinciples.title: Stay ahead of technology.
operatingPrinciples.description: Learn emerging technology before it becomes an expectation.

operatingPrinciples.title: Find the interesting question first.
operatingPrinciples.description: The best writing begins with curiosity rather than keywords.

operatingPrinciples.title: Prefer evidence over assumptions.
operatingPrinciples.description: Research, interviews and measurable outcomes should support important conclusions.

operatingPrinciples.title: Leave every project better documented than you found it.
operatingPrinciples.description: Future work should become easier because today's work was well organized.

careerPhilosophy.definitionOfSuccess: Success is becoming increasingly valuable because of knowledge, adaptability and judgment rather than a specific job title.
careerPhilosophy.primaryMotivation: Continuous learning and building meaningful work.

careerStrategy.summary: Rather than chasing titles, Riley follows industries, technologies and opportunities where communication can create measurable impact.
beliefs: Skills outlast job titles.
Technology changes faster than careers.
Communication remains valuable regardless of industry.
AI is an amplifier, not a replacement.

longTermGoals: Become recognized as a leader in AI-assisted communication.
Build intelligent systems that automate repetitive creative work.
Develop products instead of relying solely on employment income.
Continue learning faster than the market changes.

decisionMakingFramework.summary: Decisions are made by balancing curiosity, evidence, long-term value and practicality rather than short-term convenience.

process.title: Understand the real problem
process.description: Avoid solving symptoms. Spend time identifying the underlying issue before proposing solutions.

process.title: Gather context
process.description: Research, interview stakeholders and understand constraints before committing to an approach.

process.title: Prefer elegant simplicity
process.description: Choose the simplest solution that remains scalable and maintainable.

process.title: Think in systems
process.description: Whenever possible, solve classes of problems instead of isolated problems.

process.title: Leave room for iteration
process.description: Rarely assume the first solution is the final solution. Build with continuous improvement in mind.

currentFocus: Continue expanding practical AI engineering experience.
growthAreas.belief: Growth comes from deliberate practice and curiosity rather than perfection.

coreMotivators.name: Continuous Learning
coreMotivators.description: The opportunity to learn something genuinely new is one of the strongest drivers of engagement.

coreMotivators.name: Building Systems
coreMotivators.description: Prefers creating tools, frameworks and processes that continue producing value long after they are finished.

coreMotivators.name: Problem Solving
coreMotivators.description: Enjoys untangling complicated problems and designing elegant solutions.

coreMotivators.name: Meaningful Communication
coreMotivators.description: Finds satisfaction in helping other people understand ideas they previously found confusing.

coreMotivators.name: Discovery
coreMotivators.description: Naturally investigates unfamiliar subjects simply because they are interesting.

idealWorkEnvironment.summary: Riley performs best in organizations that value autonomy, curiosity and collaboration over hierarchy.
teamCharacteristics: People who value curiosity over certainty.

leadershipPhilosophy.summary: Leadership is creating an environment where people discover what they do best and become confident doing it.
beliefs: Every person has different motivations.
Managers should understand those motivations.
Confidence grows through ownership.
People perform better when they understand why their work matters.
Coaching creates stronger teams than control.

mentoringPhilosophy.summary: The goal is not to create copies of yourself. The goal is to help people become the best version of themselves.
principles: Create opportunities aligned with those strengths.
Teach people how to think rather than what to think.
mentoringPhilosophy.successDefinition: Someone leaves the team more capable and more confident than when they arrived.

approach: Focus on solving the problem rather than assigning blame.
Use evidence instead of emotion whenever possible.
Leave the relationship stronger than before.

learningPhilosophy.summary: Learning is a permanent competitive advantage. Skills become outdated; the ability to learn quickly does not.
coreBeliefs: Every project should teach something new.
Technology should be explored before it becomes mandatory.
Knowledge becomes more valuable when documented.
Understanding first principles creates better long-term judgment.

learningMethods.description: Read broadly before forming opinions. Understand context rather than memorizing facts.
Build real projects instead of consuming endless tutorials.
Explaining ideas to others exposes weaknesses in personal understanding.
Compare unrelated industries to identify transferable ideas.

technologyPhilosophy.summary: Technology should remove repetitive work so people can spend more time thinking, creating and solving meaningful problems.
beliefs: AI is a tool, not an identity.
Early adaptation creates opportunity.
Automation should increase quality as well as speed.
The best technology feels invisible.
Human judgment remains the final layer of quality control.
technologyPhilosophy.longTermVision: Create intelligent systems that continuously improve through accumulated knowledge rather than repeated manual effort.

communicationPhilosophy.purpose: Communication exists to reduce confusion, increase understanding and create trust.
principles: Assume the audience is intelligent but unfamiliar with the topic.
Clarity is more important than sounding impressive.
Every explanation should reduce cognitive effort.
Good communication respects the reader's time.
writingGoals: Help readers feel smarter after reading.

editorialPhilosophy.summary: The strongest content begins with genuine curiosity and ends with practical understanding.
beliefs: Interesting questions create interesting articles.
Research should deepen understanding, not inflate word count.
Every article should have one central idea.
Editing is where writing becomes valuable.
Readers remember stories more than explanations.
articleFramework: Remove anything that does not support the central idea.

creativePhilosophy.summary: Creativity is the process of combining existing ideas into something more useful than either idea alone.
beliefs: Originality often comes from unexpected combinations.
Constraints encourage better thinking.
Curiosity fuels creativity.
Systems increase creative output rather than reducing it.
Documentation preserves creative momentum.

professionalDecisionHeuristics.summary: Default rules Riley naturally follows when making professional decisions.

heuristics.title: Optimize for learning.
heuristics.description: When two opportunities appear similar, choose the one that teaches the most.

heuristics.title: Build reusable assets.
heuristics.description: Prefer creating something that can be reused hundreds of times over solving a problem once.

heuristics.title: Compounding beats intensity.
heuristics.description: Consistent improvement produces larger long-term results than occasional bursts of effort.

heuristics.title: Reduce friction.
heuristics.description: Whenever possible, remove unnecessary steps rather than simply working faster.

heuristics.title: Always ask why.
heuristics.description: Understanding intent produces better solutions than simply executing instructions.

heuristics.title: Leave behind knowledge.
heuristics.description: Every project should improve future projects through documentation or automation.
